metadata.icdo_version: ICD-O-3.2. morphology_entries[] is GENERATED by build/generate_group_inventory.py --group V from ICCC-2017.sqlite joined to icdo32.sqlite, never transcribed from an option file or a diagnostic pathway document (Group 5 build contract Sec.1). Two codes on this stem are absent from this file, and neither absence is a deletion: 9510/0 Retinocytoma exists and is current in ICD-O-3.2 but is coded at behaviour 0, outside ICCC-3 Group V's behaviour-3 declaration (contract Sec.0.2, Sec.2.1); 9514/1 Retinoblastoma, spontaneously regressed exists and is current in ICD-O-3.2 at behaviour 1 only — ICD-O-3.2 carries no 9514/3 — and is likewise outside the declaration (contract Sec.0.2, Sec.2.2). The generator's own summary line records codes_absent_from_icdo32: ['9514'], meaning ICD-O-3.2 carries no 9514/3, not that 9514 is missing from ICD-O-3.2 altogether — the identical mechanism that kept 8683 out of Group IV (Group 4 contract Sec.0.2). Both codes are recorded only inside a behaviour_exclusion block in this file (rb_enucleation_report), never as a morphology_code. All four IARC 3.1-to-3.2 change documents were searched for '951[0-9]', 'retinoblast', 'retinocyt' and 'retinom' on 22 September 2026: no hits in any of the four, so this stem predates ICD-O-3.2 and was untouched by it (contract Sec.0.3).

morphology_entries.imaging_features: A calcified intraocular mass on B-scan ultrasound (or, when unavailable, orbital magnetic resonance imaging, which detects calcification poorly) in a child under five years, with no feature suggesting a leukocoria mimic. Razek & Elkhamary 2011; Ghose & Kaliki 2022; College of American Pathologists Retinoblastoma Protocol v4.0.0.0, Note A (build contract Sec.0.5). Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, pp. 04-05, names retinoblastoma as one of only five entities in the entire European Network of Cancer Registries scheme registrable at basis 1 (clinical examination alone) or basis 2 (clinical investigation, including imaging) with no tissue at all, topography C69.2, morphology 9510/3.
morphology_entries.coding_note: Generated by build/generate_group_inventory.py --group V from ICCC-2017.sqlite joined to icdo32.sqlite, never transcribed (build contract Sec.1). Preferred term 'Retinoblastoma, NOS', behaviour 3, confirmed in icdo32.sqlite with no [obs] marker and no see_also / see_note / includes / excludes on the stem (contract Sec.0.3). This is the dominant, modal code in the group: most retinoblastoma cases in this registry will code 9510/3, because biopsy of an intact globe is contraindicated and diagnosis is ordinarily clinical plus imaging (contract Sec.0.5). Milman T, Grossniklaus HE, Goldman-Levy G, et al. The 5th Edition of the World Health Organization Classification of Tumours of the Eye and Orbit. Ocular Oncology and Pathology 2023;9(3-4):71-95 [the copy held is the online-first version, paginated 1-25, not the bound 71-95 print pagination -- contract Sec.10.2b], Table 9, Tumours of the neurosensory retina, lists Retinoblastoma as one of four named entities -- confirming a current World Health Organization entity lives on this stem. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, pp. 04-05: Retinoblastoma is basis 1 or 2, topography C69.2, morphology 9510/3 (contract Sec.0.4). No branch in this tree may reach 9511, 9512 or 9513 without a pathology report; every basis-1 and basis-2 terminal emits 9510/3 only. who_version is recorded as 'WHO 2023', the year of the paper that classifies and names the entity on this stem, not the year the entity's behaviour was first fixed. The bound WHO Classification of Tumours, 5th edition, Volume 13: Eye and Orbit Tumours (IARC, ISBN 978-92-832-4546-9) did not reach final print until 23 January 2026, thirty-three months after the April 2023 online-first beta this paper summarises, and no published comparison of the two exists -- whether the retina chapter changed between them is not established (contract Sec.10.2, registrar item Sec.11.7). code_neutral_molecular is true: RB1 germline status, MYCN amplification and chromosome 6p gain drive counselling and prognosis, not the code -- hereditary and sporadic retinoblastoma both code 9510/3 (contract Sec.0.5, fact 3). CORRECTED 2026-09-22 by the build controller. This entry previously declared diagnostic_tests_required ['Histology']. 9510 is the imaging-sufficient code and is reached with no tissue on the modal path, so the engine computed Histology as an OUTSTANDING test and wrote its own upgrade sentence, 'Histology would yield a more specific code.', onto a case with an intact globe — inviting a contraindicated procedure and misreporting the case as incompletely worked up. Build contract Sec.5.4 maps examination under anaesthesia, ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging all onto 'Imaging'; Sec.5.5 bans the missing-test framing outright. upgrade_path is authored so app.js's automatic sentence (app.js outcome assembly, `auto`) never fires on any 9510 terminal.
morphology_entries.upgrade_path: The only more specific codes in this group — 9511 differentiated, 9512 undifferentiated, 9513 diffuse — are read off an enucleation or exenteration pathology report. Enucleation is a TREATMENT decision, not an outstanding investigation: biopsy of an eye that still contains the tumour is contraindicated and risks spreading it outside the eye. Do not record this case as incompletely worked up because no histology exists, and do not request tissue on account of this code.

morphology_entries.coding_note: Generated by build/generate_group_inventory.py --group V (contract Sec.1). Preferred term 'Retinoblastoma, differentiated', behaviour 3, a live, non-obsolete term in icdo32.sqlite, untouched by all four IARC 3.1-to-3.2 change documents (contract Sec.0.3). Milman T, et al. Ocular Oncology and Pathology 2023;9(3-4):71-95 [online-first copy held, paginated 1-25 -- contract Sec.10.2b], Table 9, lists exactly four entities under Tumours of the neurosensory retina -- Astrocytic tumours, Nodular and massive retinal gliosis, Retinocytoma, Retinoblastoma -- and names no separate 'differentiated' or 'undifferentiated' type. The paper's own Table 2 defines Type, Subtype and Pattern, and its Table 1 shows Subtypes are a subsection inside an entity's own section, not an entry in the chapter's type list -- so Table 9's silence shows only that this is not a separate type; it says nothing about whether a World Health Organization subtype carrying its own ICD-O code sits inside the Retinoblastoma entity page, which is paywalled and was not read (contract Sec.10.3). The paper states no ICD-O code anywhere in twenty-five pages (contract Sec.10.2b) -- a paper that prints no code cannot retire one. This code is therefore retained -- ICD-O-3.2 prints it as a live, non-obsolete Preferred term and it is a REDCap option -- and reachable only from the pathology report's own stated differentiation grade or growth pattern, the Group 4 D3 precedent on comparable evidence (contract Sec.2.4, Sec.10.3). who_version is recorded as 'ICD-O-3.2', not a World Health Organization edition: no current World Health Organization entity has been confirmed on this stem (registrar item Sec.11.5). Mapping, from the College of American Pathologists Retinoblastoma Protocol v4.0.0.0 (2017) and contract Sec.2.4: fleurette formation or neuronal differentiation (grade G1); numerous Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes, moderately differentiated (grade G2); or, on Mendoza's anaplasia scale (Mendoza PR, et al. Histopathologic grading of anaplasia in retinoblastoma. American Journal of Ophthalmology 2015;159(4):764-776), a retinocytoma-grade area or mild anaplasia recorded within an otherwise viable retinoblastoma -- not a standalone retinocytoma, which is 9510/0 and behaviour-excluded (contract Sec.2.1, Sec.2.3). code_neutral_molecular is true (contract Sec.0.5).

Generated by build/generate_group_inventory.py --group V (contract Sec.1). Preferred term 'Retinoblastoma, undifferentiated', behaviour 3, a live, non-obsolete term in icdo32.sqlite (contract Sec.0.3). Milman 2023 Table 9 names no separate 'undifferentiated' type on the retinoblastoma stem (see the 9511 entry's coding_note for the full reasoning; it applies identically here). The paper prints no ICD-O code anywhere, so it cannot retire one (contract Sec.10.2b); the code is retained on ICD-O-3.2's own authority and reachable only from the pathology report's own stated wording (contract Sec.2.4). who_version recorded as 'ICD-O-3.2': no current World Health Organization entity has been confirmed on this stem (registrar item Sec.11.5). Mapping, from the College of American Pathologists Retinoblastoma Protocol v4.0.0.0 (2017) and contract Sec.2.4: occasional rosettes, poorly differentiated (grade G3); no rosettes present, anaplasia, poorly differentiated (grade G4); or, on Mendoza's anaplasia scale (Mendoza PR, et al. American Journal of Ophthalmology 2015;159(4):764-776), severe anaplasia. Mendoza 2015 also records that severe anaplasia independently flags metastatic risk even with no standard high-risk histopathological feature present -- a clinical consequence, not a coding one, and recorded in docs/clinical-warnings.md, not here (contract Sec.9). code_neutral_molecular is true (contract Sec.0.5).

Generated by build/generate_group_inventory.py --group V (contract Sec.1). Preferred term 'Retinoblastoma, diffuse', behaviour 3, a live, non-obsolete term in icdo32.sqlite (contract Sec.0.3). Milman 2023 Table 9 names no separate 'diffuse' type on the retinoblastoma stem; growth pattern (endophytic, exophytic, mixed, diffuse infiltrating) most likely sits at the paper's own Table 2 third level, pattern, below subtype -- not established either way, since the entity page that would confirm it is paywalled (contract Sec.10.3). The code is retained on ICD-O-3.2's own authority and reachable only from the enucleation report's own stated growth pattern (contract Sec.2.4). who_version recorded as 'ICD-O-3.2': no current World Health Organization entity has been confirmed on this stem (registrar item Sec.11.5). imaging_sufficient is false here and false nowhere else matters as much: diffuse infiltrating retinoblastoma grows as a flat placoid infiltrate without a discrete calcified mass, is rare, presents later (around age six), and mimics uveitis or endophthalmitis, so the imaging-pathway's own calcified-mass and under-five criteria would falsely exclude it (contract Sec.2.5) -- this code is enucleation-only. code_neutral_molecular is true (contract Sec.0.5).

decision_trees.tree_label: Retinoblastoma (C69.0-C69.9 eye and adnexa; ICCC-3 Group V declares behaviour 3 at any site) — the imaging-first pathway, cytology and liquid biopsy, and the enucleation/exenteration report's own subtype wording

nodes.question: What is in this patient's file?
nodes.hint: Biopsy of an eye that still contains the tumour is avoided, because incisional or needle biopsy risks seeding the tumour outside the eye. A pathology report therefore exists only once the eye itself has been removed as treatment. The next step records which imaging was performed.

items.label: Imaging report
items.about: Eye examination under anaesthesia, ultrasound or orbital magnetic resonance imaging.

items.label: Cytology report
items.about: Cells from a needle aspirate or a fluid sample, read under the microscope.

items.label: Liquid biopsy report
items.about: Tumour DNA from the aqueous humour or from plasma.

items.label: Histology report
items.about: A pathology report on an enucleation or exenteration specimen.

nodes.coding_note: Tree architecture per build contract Sec.4: five routes off this node. The contract's own diagram lists the fifth route's (inadequate/uninterpretable specimen) destination as 'rb_imaging_pathway or the non-registrable terminal' without deciding between them. This build routes it to rb_imaging_pathway: a failed tissue attempt does not erase whatever clinical/imaging evidence is also in the file, so that evidence is checked against the full constellation before the case falls through the pathway's own insufficient_next_node (rb_imaging_insufficient) to a non-reportable or Group XII outcome. Registrar rulings, 14 October 2026: (RQ7) the list carries only the three documents that decide a route here, so a referral letter, laboratory results, an immunohistochemistry report and a genetic test report are not offered, and a file with none of the four boxes ticked is the referral tier; (RP4) a liquid biopsy report is its own box and fits the cytology tier, whose answer is basis of diagnosis 5 (Visser 2023 rule 8, p. 06); (RP6) a specimen reported inadequate means no histological diagnosis, so the inadequate row wins over a ticked histology report and warns the clerk about the discrepancy (tick_conflict). The list is this node's own, not the shared vocabulary's: the shared list is drawn on every group's first screen, and a liquid biopsy box that changes no route elsewhere would be the kind of box RQ7 removed here.

options.label: Referral letter or clinical note only — no ophthalmic examination or imaging report, no cytology or liquid biopsy, no pathology report in the file
Ophthalmic examination under anaesthesia, B-scan ultrasound, and/or orbital magnetic resonance imaging report — the eye is intact, no cytology or liquid biopsy, no pathology report
Cytology report, or an aqueous-humour or plasma liquid biopsy report — no enucleation or exenteration specimen in the file
Enucleation or exenteration specimen with a pathology report
A specimen was taken but reported inadequate or non-diagnostic

tick_conflict.notice: A histology report is ticked, and the specimen is also marked inadequate. An inadequate specimen gives no histological diagnosis, so this case continues without the histology report. If the report is usable, choose "None of these" instead.

nodes.question: Tick everything the referral letter or clinical note states.
nodes.hint: Tick only what the note itself states. A note that only describes a mass, a red-reflex abnormality or a request for eye examination states none of these. Leukocoria is a white pupillary reflex, or a cat's-eye reflex. Strabismus counts only with a suspected intraocular tumour of the retina. A non-malignant cause, such as Coats disease or persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous, outranks every other tick and makes the case not reportable. Leave it unticked when the note names none.

items.label: Strabismus with a suspected tumour of the retina
A non-malignant cause is named, such as Coats disease
items.about: A cause that could equally explain the findings.

tick_list.label: Note states
tick_list.prompt: Tick every finding the note states. Tick none if it states none.

nodes.coding_note: Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, pp. 04-05: retinoblastoma is one of only five entities in the entire European Network of Cancer Registries scheme registrable at basis 1, clinical examination alone, with no imaging and no tissue (build contract Sec.0.4, Sec.4). Basis 1 is legal here specifically because it is guarded by group in the validator and Table 3 names retinoblastoma's row '1 or 2' -- the ban that applies to Group 3 does not apply to Group 5 (contract Sec.0.6). Rule 4, p. 03: 'possible is not registrable' -- if clinical investigation makes cancer only possible, or a non-malignant disorder could equally explain the findings, the case is not registered at all in the absence of pathology; this is a non_reportable destination, not a refer_group one, because Coats disease and persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous are not cancers in any group (contract Sec.0.4 point 4). Registrar ruling, 14 October 2026 (RQ3): a non-malignant cause named in the note, such as Coats disease, wins over every other finding, so the screen is a tick list read in file order with that item first. The note often says nothing about Coats disease; an unticked box leaves the other findings to decide. Registrar ruling, 14 October 2026 (RP1): this screen is also the third rung of the fall-through, reached from rb_imaging_insufficient when imaging gave no usable feature and the file holds a referral note.

options.label: A non-malignant cause is named
options.reason: Cancer is only possible, not at least likely, on the note's own wording, or a non-malignant disorder could equally explain the findings. Under Visser 2023 rule 4 (p. 03), this is not registered at all in the absence of pathology.

options.label: Note names retinoblastoma, or describes leukocoria or strabismus with a suspected tumour
options.reason: Retinoblastoma is one of only five entities in the entire European Network of Cancer Registries scheme that may be registered on clinical examination alone, with no imaging and no tissue (Visser O, et al., Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, pp. 04-05). Recorded as Retinoblastoma, NOS (9510/3) at basis of diagnosis 1.

options.label: No diagnosis stated
options.reason: Cancer is only possible, not at least likely, on the note's own wording, or a non-malignant disorder could equally explain the findings. Under Visser 2023 rule 4 (p. 03), this is not registered at all in the absence of pathology.

nodes.question: Tick every feature the eye examination and imaging report state.
nodes.hint: Calcification within the mass is the discriminator and is not optional. Leukocoria causes retinoblastoma in only 56-72% of children; the rest is Coats disease, persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous, coloboma, sclerosing endophthalmitis, retinal astrocytoma, Norrie disease, retinopathy of prematurity and medulloepithelioma (Razek & Elkhamary 2011), and those mimics characteristically show no calcified mass. Ultrasound, not magnetic resonance imaging, detects calcification: magnetic resonance imaging detects it poorly, and computed tomography is avoided in children at risk of a germline tumour-suppressor mutation. Record whichever imaging was performed.
imaging_features: An intraocular mass on B-scan ultrasound or on orbital magnetic resonance imaging
Calcification within the mass (high-reflectivity foci casting acoustic shadows)
Child under five years of age

diversion_criteria.feature: Retinal detachment or exudate with no calcified mass
diversion_criteria.reason: Matches the Coats disease or persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous pattern rather than retinoblastoma. A non-malignant disorder could equally explain the findings, and under Visser 2023 rule 4 (p. 03) the case is not registered without pathology.

diversion_criteria.feature: A flat, diffusely infiltrating intraocular process with no discrete mass
diversion_criteria.reason: Matches diffuse infiltrating retinoblastoma, which grows without a discrete calcified mass and presents later than typical retinoblastoma. The calcified-mass and under-five criteria above would wrongly exclude it. This constellation needs tissue, not exclusion.

Pseudohypopyon is the commonest presentation of diffuse infiltrating retinoblastoma, which grows without a discrete calcified mass (Razek and Elkhamary 2011, p. 2). It also occurs with inflammation, so this needs tissue, not exclusion.

Suggests an inflammatory mimic such as endophthalmitis or uveitis. A non-malignant disorder could equally explain the findings, and under Visser 2023 rule 4 (p. 03) the case is not registered without pathology.

Changes the specimen that will arrive — an exenteration rather than a straightforward enucleation, or treatment before any specimen exists — so the case is directed to await that tissue rather than registered on imaging alone.

nodes.coding_note: Engine constraint (build contract Sec.0.6, docs/TODO.md Sec.10): imagingPathway() renders only imaging_features, biochemical_questions and diversion_criteria -- options[] is never rendered. This node therefore declares insufficient_next_node, does not declare options[], and carries its own morphology_code/behavior_code/basis_of_diagnosis for the confirmed-constellation outcome. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, pp. 04-05: retinoblastoma is basis 2 on clinical investigation (imaging) with no tissue -- the modal output of the whole group (contract Sec.0.4 point 2). Diversion criteria per contract Sec.4.1: two patterns (no calcified mass; anterior-segment/inflammatory picture) point to a non-malignant mimic and are not registered without pathology (Visser rule 4, p. 03); two patterns (diffuse-infiltrating/older child; extraocular or orbital extension) still need tissue and must not be read as 'not cancer' (contract Sec.2.5, Sec.4.1) -- rb_imaging_insufficient carries that distinction forward. Registrar ruling, 14 October 2026 (RP2): pseudohypopyon is the commonest presentation of diffuse infiltrating retinoblastoma (Razek and Elkhamary 2011, p. 2), so it is its own box and, on the next screen, reads as a pattern that needs tissue; build contract Sec.4.1 and Sec.2.5, which sent it to the mimic answer, are amended. An anterior-segment mass stays with the inflammatory mimics.

nodes.step_label: Imaging did not confirm — what next
nodes.question: The imaging did not confirm retinoblastoma. Tick what the file shows.
nodes.hint: The patterns are not equivalent. Retinal detachment or exudate with no calcified mass is the Coats disease or persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous pattern, and an anterior-segment mass points to an inflammatory mimic: with no pathology, neither is registered. Pseudohypopyon, a diffuse infiltrating pattern, an older child or extraocular extension is still a real possibility of retinoblastoma and needs tissue, not exclusion. If the file shows a mimic pattern and a pattern that needs tissue together, the tool takes tissue, so that no possible cancer is dropped. When no imaging feature is usable, tick the referral letter or clinical note if the file holds one: it is read next.

items.label: Needs tissue: diffuse pattern, pseudohypopyon, age five or older, or extraocular extension
Mimic pattern: detachment or exudate with no calcified mass, or an anterior-segment mass
A referral letter or clinical note is in the file
items.about: Read next when no required imaging feature is stated.

tick_list.label: Imaging shows
tick_list.prompt: Tick every finding that applies. Tick none if no required feature is stated.

nodes.coding_note: Reached only from rb_imaging_pathway's insufficient_next_node. Build contract Sec.4.1: the diversion criteria send a case to tissue, which is the correct outcome, not to a 'not cancer' terminal, so the diffuse-variant, older-child and extraocular-extension patterns route to refer_group 12 (an honest 'pending tissue' state), never to non_reportable. The non-calcified and anterior-segment patterns are the genuine Visser rule 4 case (p. 03): a non-malignant disorder could equally explain the findings, so the case is not registered without pathology. Registrar rulings, 14 October 2026: (RQ1) the two answers 'tissue has since been obtained' are removed, because the first screen already records which reports are in the file and a clerk with a new report goes back to it; (RP2) pseudohypopyon is a pattern that needs tissue (Razek and Elkhamary 2011, p. 2); (RP3) with a required feature missing the case is a suspected neoplasm, Group XII provisional; (RP1) the fall through takes the rungs in order, cytology, imaging, referral wording, each coding what its evidence supports: when no imaging feature is usable and the file holds a referral note, the note is read (rb_clinical_alias). A mimic pattern or a pattern that needs tissue does not fall through, because the imaging itself says what the findings are; the note's own rule (Visser 2023 rule 4, p. 03) would otherwise be overruled by a wording the imaging contradicts. (RQ4) when the imaging shows both a mimic pattern and a pattern that needs tissue, tissue wins (registrar ruling, 14 October 2026, option A): no possible cancer is dropped. The screen is therefore a tick list read in file order, tissue first, then mimic, then the referral note, then nothing. No paper holds that magnetic resonance imaging plus clinical suspicion registers a case when a mimic pattern is also present: Visser 2023 (Table 3, pp. 04-05) registers retinoblastoma on clinical investigation alone but rule 4 (p. 03) excludes a case a non-malignant disorder could equally explain; Foerl B, et al. Ophthalmologe 2008;105(8):761-764 (PubMed 18299842) enucleated two eyes whose examination under anaesthesia, magnetic resonance imaging and ultrasound could not exclude retinoblastoma and found Coats disease; Nelson AJ, et al. Case Rep Ophthalmol 2025;16(1):366-371 (PubMed 40469936) turns to an aqueous liquid biopsy when examination and imaging cannot diagnose or exclude it.

Record it provisionally under Group XII (8000/3, malignant neoplasm, NOS) pending cytology, a liquid biopsy, or an enucleation/exenteration specimen.

A required feature is not stated, and no referral letter or clinical note is in the file

nodes.question: What does the cytology or liquid-biopsy report show?
nodes.hint: Biopsy of an intact globe is avoided because of the risk of extraocular seeding. Diagnostic features of malignancy — necrosis, mitoses and nuclear atypia — should be present before retinoblastoma is diagnosed on a cytology. Sampling of retinal neurons and scant material are the two pitfalls that can mislead a cytological read; consultation with an experienced ophthalmic cytopathologist is recommended when a biopsy is considered. A cytology cannot grade differentiation or establish a growth pattern, so it never yields a subtype. A liquid biopsy of the aqueous humour or plasma counts when it reports a change specific to the tumour, such as an RB1 variant or a copy-number alteration; it never yields a subtype either.
nodes.coding_note: Added once the baseline paper was on disk (build contract Sec.4, Sec.10.9). Milman T, et al. Ocular Oncology and Pathology 2023;9(3-4):71-95 [online-first copy held, paginated 1-25], Table 10, Diagnostic cytology of tumours of the retina and neuroepithelium, verbatim: 'Generally, biopsy is avoided due to the risk of extraocular recurrence and metastasis. Cytological samples often have pitfalls (sampling of retinal neurons, scant material) that may be misleading. Diagnostic features of malignancy such as necrosis, mitoses, and nuclear atypia should be present when diagnosing retinoblastoma in a cytology. Consultation with an experienced ophthalmic cytopathologist is recommended if a biopsy is considered.' Read carefully: avoided, with conditions attached for when it is done, not never done. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 1 (p. 03): cytology is basis 5, stronger than the imaging route's basis 2. Rule 8, p. 06: an aqueous-humour or plasma liquid biopsy is basis 5 as well, not 8, whenever no pathology is available, even when it finds a cancer-specific genetic abnormality. 'Cytology' is used here as the evidence_tests tag; the closed diagnostic_tests_required vocabulary on morphology_entries[] (Referral only / Histology / Imaging / IHC / ISH / Flow cytometry / Cytogenetics-FISH / Molecular-PCR) has no literal cytology entry, so morphology_entries[9510].diagnostic_tests_required is left at ['Histology'] and this branch-level tag is a free-form tracking value, not a closed-list field. Registrar ruling, 14 October 2026 (RP4): a liquid biopsy report is its own box on the first screen and reaches this screen. Its positive answer is basis of diagnosis 5 (Visser 2023 rule 8, p. 06, whenever no pathology is available, even when it finds a cancer-specific genetic abnormality). Ghose N, Kaliki S. Seminars in Ophthalmology 2022;37:813-819, p. 3: aqueous-humour cell-free DNA is a surrogate marker for somatic copy-number alterations and other genetic alterations in retinoblastoma. The 'Cytology' tag is kept as the evidence_tests value for both answers, as above.

options.label: Malignant cells consistent with retinoblastoma, with necrosis, mitoses or nuclear atypia
options.reason: Cells consistent with retinoblastoma are present on cytology, at European Network of Cancer Registries basis of diagnosis 5. A cytology cannot grade differentiation or establish a growth pattern, so this is recorded as Retinoblastoma, NOS (9510/3), never a subtype.
options.coding_note: satisfies_tests ['Imaging'] added 2026-09-22: a cytology or liquid-biopsy report is ENCR basis 5, above the basis 2 the imaging constellation carries (Visser 2023, Table 1). Imaging is not an outstanding test on a case that already has cells, and leaving it outstanding would have printed 'Imaging would yield a more specific code.' — which is untrue: imaging yields no more specific code in this group at all.

options.label: Liquid biopsy reports a tumour-specific genetic change
options.reason: A liquid biopsy of the aqueous humour or plasma reports a change specific to the tumour, at European Network of Cancer Registries basis of diagnosis 5 (Visser 2023, rule 8, p. 06). It cannot grade differentiation or establish a growth pattern, so this is recorded as Retinoblastoma, NOS (9510/3), never a subtype.

options.label: Non-diagnostic: scant material, retinal neurons only, or nothing specific to the tumour
options.coding_note: Corrected 14 October 2026 (branch reach-g05, neutral recheck TOOL_SHORT). This answer used to end at a Group XII referral and never looked at an imaging report in the same file. Build contract Sec.4 (note on the fifth route of rb_document_inventory): a failed tissue attempt does not erase the clinical or imaging evidence also in the file, so that evidence is checked against the full constellation before the case falls through to a non-reportable or Group XII outcome. A non-diagnostic cytology is the same situation as the first screen's inadequate-specimen row and now takes the same route, with the same captures. Registrar ruling 11 (4 September 2026): an uninterpretable test drops the case to the nearest code, never to a dead end. A case with no imaging evidence ends where it did before: the imaging screen, then 'Needs tissue', then the Group XII referral.

nodes.question: Tick every finding the pathology report states about the tumour.
nodes.hint: Code from the report's own wording; do not infer a grade or growth pattern. Differentiated is grade G1 (fleurette formation or neuronal differentiation) or G2 (numerous Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes), or mild anaplasia on the Mendoza scale. Poorly differentiated or undifferentiated is grade G3 (occasional rosettes) or G4 (no rosettes with anaplasia), or severe anaplasia. Where the report states more than one finding, the tool takes the highest: diffuse growth, then poorly differentiated or undifferentiated, then differentiated. Moderate anaplasia alone changes no code. Enucleation is the treatment that produced this specimen, not an outstanding investigation: nothing further needs to be removed from the child to read a fuller report on tissue already in hand.

items.label: Diffuse infiltrating growth
items.about: The tumour spreads within the retina with no discrete mass.

items.label: Retinocytoma or retinoma as an area inside a viable retinoblastoma
items.about: A retinocytomatous area: the lowest grade on the Mendoza scale.

items.label: The whole specimen is retinocytoma or retinoma, with no viable retinoblastoma

tick_list.label: Report states

nodes.coding_note: Mapping per College of American Pathologists Retinoblastoma Protocol v4.0.0.0 (2017) and build contract Sec.2.4. Registrar rulings, 14 October 2026: (RQ2) the enucleation screen and the retinocytoma-meaning screen are one tick screen, read in file order, first fit wins; (RQ6) a report that says 'retinocytoma-grade area' is the 'area' box, so it is read as an area inside a viable tumour and codes 9511 unless a poorer grade or a diffuse pattern is also ticked. The order is the precedence the old hint stated: diffuse growth (9513, the higher code; Rule K, registrar's decision of 7 October 2026), then poorly differentiated or undifferentiated (9512), then differentiated or a retinocytoma-grade area (9511), then a whole-specimen retinocytoma (9510/0, outside the group's behaviour), then phthisis bulbi (9514/1), then no stated grade (9510/3). Where a report states more than one grade the higher governs (registrar's decision, 7 October 2026): the WHO ICD-O-3 first revision, section 4.3.4, pp. 21-22, assigns the higher of two stated degrees and sets 'anaplastic' at grade IV beside 'undifferentiated'; the College of American Pathologists protocol, p. 4, and Mendoza 2015, p. 765, grade anaplasia on its highest level in the tumour. Severe anaplasia therefore outranks G1 and G2. Moderate anaplasia alone, and a report stating nothing, take the last option as the conservative, least-specific default (flagged for the registrar, not resolved by the contract). A ticked 'area' beside a ticked 'whole' is read as an area inside a viable tumour (9511), the direction that keeps a malignancy registered. Retinocytoma homonym, build contract Sec.2.3: coding a retinocytomatous area within an active retinoblastoma as 9510/0 would record a benign tumour for a child who has a malignant one. Mendoza PR, et al. American Journal of Ophthalmology 2015;159(4):764-776 runs the anaplasia scale retinocytoma/mild/moderate/severe inside an active retinoblastoma. Al-Hussaini M, et al. International Journal of Retina and Vitreous 2025;11:20, confirms 9510/0 as the ICD-O code for standalone retinocytoma. Milman 2023 records that the World Health Organization classifies retinocytoma as premalignant while ICD-O-3.2 codes it 9510/0, behaviour 0 (benign); the behaviour code is IARC's, not the World Health Organization's, and the tool codes to ICD-O-3.2 (contract Sec.10.4). That divergence is a registrar item (Sec.11.6).

options.label: Diffuse infiltrating growth
Poorly differentiated or undifferentiated
Differentiated, or a retinocytoma-grade area in a viable tumour
Retinocytoma or retinoma only: no viable retinoblastoma

behaviour_exclusion.reason: Retinocytoma (retinoma) is the benign counterpart of retinoblastoma. ICD-O-3.2 codes it 9510/0. ICCC-3 Group V admits behaviour 3 only, so it is not a registrable cancer in this group and no Group V code is emitted for it. Record the finding and refer the case to the registrar.

options.label: Phthisis bulbi with no viable tumour

behaviour_exclusion.reason: A spontaneously regressed retinoblastoma is the shrunken, calcified, non-functional globe (phthisis bulbi) with no viable tumour. ICD-O-3.2 codes it 9514/1. ICCC-3 Group V admits behaviour 3 only, so it is not a registrable cancer in this group and no Group V code is emitted for it. Whether the registry registers a regressed retinoblastoma as an incident case, and on what code, is a registration-rules question for the registrar, not a morphology question this tool can settle. Record the finding and refer the case to the registrar.

options.label: No grade and no growth pattern stated
options.reason: The enucleation specimen confirms retinoblastoma, but the report states no differentiation grade and no growth pattern. Recorded as Retinoblastoma, NOS (9510/3). A fuller reading of the same specimen stating a grade or growth pattern would allow this case to move to a specific subtype; nothing further needs to be removed from the child to get that detail.
